components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main continue, preview, or export action in the current station.
components.css: .ds-button-primary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 46px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid #00d4ff; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; background: #00d4ff; color: #001a20; cursor: pointer; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-button-primary:hover:not(:disabled) { background: #5ee4ff; color: #001318; } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffd166; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-button-primary:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.45; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A reversible or supporting action that remains visible beside the primary action.
components.css: .ds-button-secondary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 46px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid rgba(230, 237, 243, 0.3); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; background: #1e2535; color: #e6edf3; cursor: pointer; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-button-secondary:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: #00d4ff; background: #253044; } .ds-button-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffd166; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-button-secondary:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.45; }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.description: A low-emphasis reset, exit, or back action that should not compete with forward progress.
components.css: .ds-button-quiet { display: inline-flex; min-height: 46px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid rgba(230, 237, 243, 0.3); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; background: transparent; color: #e6edf3; cursor: pointer; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-button-quiet:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: #00d4ff; background: #253044; } .ds-button-quiet:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffd166; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-button-quiet:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.45; }

components.name: Text Field

components.css: .ds-field { display: block; max-width: 520px; color: #e6edf3; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { display: block; margin-bottom: 9px; font-size: 0.79rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-field-input { width: 100%; min-height: 48px; border: 1px solid rgba(230, 237, 243, 0.3); border-radius: 8px; padding: 11px 14px; background: #111722; color: #e6edf3; font: 1rem Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-field-input::placeholder { color: #8193a4; } .ds-field-input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffd166; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-field-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: #ff8b8b; } .ds-field-help { display: block; margin-top: 8px; color: #aebdcb; font-size: 0.76rem; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Station Navigation
components.description: A continuous numbered rail showing resting, completed, and active creation stations.
components.css: .ds-stations { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(110px, 1fr)); overflow-x: auto; border: 1px solid rgba(230, 237, 243, 0.16); background: #111722; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-station { display: flex; min-height: 58px; align-items: center; gap: 10px; border: 0; border-right: 1px solid rgba(230, 237, 243, 0.16); padding: 10px 14px; background: transparent; color: #aebdcb; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; } .ds-station:last-child { border-right: 0; } .ds-station span { display: grid; width: 28px; height: 28px; flex: 0 0 28px; place-items: center; border: 1px solid rgba(230, 237, 243, 0.3); border-radius: 50%; font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 750; } .ds-station strong { font-size: 0.79rem; font-weight: 650; } .ds-station:hover { background: rgba(230, 237, 243, 0.05); color: #e6edf3; } .ds-station:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffd166; outline-offset: -3px; } .ds-station-active { background: #00d4ff; color: #001a20; } .ds-station-active:hover { background: #00d4ff; color: #001a20; } .ds-station-active span { border-color: #001a20; } .ds-station-complete span { border-color: #78e3a0; color: #78e3a0; }

components.name: Choice Card
components.description: A full-target radio choice for templates, themes, and comfort profiles.
components.css: .ds-choice { position: relative; display: flex; min-height: 72px; align-items: center; gap: 14px; border: 1px solid rgba(230, 237, 243, 0.16); border-radius: 10px; padding: 14px 16px; background: #111722; color: #e6edf3; cursor: pointer; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-choice:hover { border-color: rgba(230, 237, 243, 0.3); } .ds-choice:has(input:checked) { border-color: #00d4ff; background: rgba(0, 212, 255, 0.07); } .ds-choice:focus-within { outline: 3px solid #ffd166; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-choice input { width: 18px; height: 18px; flex: 0 0 18px; accent-color: #00d4ff; } .ds-choice strong { display: block; margin-bottom: 3px; font-size: 0.88rem; } .ds-choice small { display: block; color: #aebdcb; font-size: 0.76rem; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Preview Status Chip
components.description: A compact live text status for the persistent preview state.

narrative.overview:
UESL is expressed as a calm night workbench where the interface stays legible, the live artifact remains visible, and progress feels coached rather than controlled. Density is purposeful: status, decision, and response share one frame, while advanced mechanics recede until the participant asks for them.

The system is direct, tool-like, and game-aware. It rejects both marketing-page spectacle and the wall of controls associated with professional editors. The workbench chrome stays stable while the miniature game world supplies the color, movement, and delight, so users can always distinguish the tool from the thing they are making.
keyCharacteristics: A four-layer navy surface stack with crisp one-pixel dividers.
Cyan active states, purple secondary markers, and gold focus cues.
Condensed Oswald headings paired with highly readable Inter body text.
One persistent preview that changes in place with every meaningful choice.
Square outer frames, gently rounded controls, and circular progress markers.
Accessibility states that visibly change motion, contrast, and control size.

rules.name: The Cyan Means Action Rule
rules.body: Cyan is reserved for current progress, selected configuration, primary actions, and navigable links; it should not wash large passive surfaces.

rules.name: The Gold Stays Legible Rule
rules.body: Gold belongs to keyboard focus and in-game landmarks, never paragraph copy.

rules.name: The Stage Palette Is Contained Rule
rules.body: Theme colors repaint the preview only; workbench chrome retains the UESL system colors.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Oswald leads page, station, and preview headings; Inter handles every instruction, status, label, and control, while monospace is reserved for literal configuration data.

rules.name: The One-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Tonal layering and one-pixel dividers do the everyday structural work; reserve the structural shadow for the complete workbench frame.

dos: Do use cyan to identify the current station, selected option, primary action, and interactive link.
Do keep the active decision and its visible outcome in the same frame.
Do preserve the 3px gold focus outline with 3px offset, direct error language, reduced-motion response, and at least 44px control targets.
Do keep the phone preview compact at 190px and above the active decision while the station rail scrolls inside its own bounds.
Do use one-pixel dividers and tonal surfaces before introducing a new shadow.
donts: Don't spread stage-theme colors into builder chrome.
Don't hide draft, restored, or session-only state behind an icon or tooltip.
Don't round the entire application into floating cards; the outer workbench remains a square, continuous frame.
Don't use Oswald for paragraphs, help text, form values, or status messages.
Don't imply server saving, publishing, or completed integration through color or copy.
